version.changelog: Add ClawHub install guidance, GitHub/registry links, and publish payload links for better discovery.

llm.summary: The skill’s files, runtime instructions, and behavior are coherent with its stated purpose (local design knowledge + code-first UI implementation); nothing in the manifest demands unrelated credentials or risky installs, but you should still review the Python scripts before letting the agent execute them autonomously.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (generate design systems and implement UI) align with included assets: a local design knowledge base (CSV/MD files) and Python scripts (search, core, design_system) to generate and map design systems into code. The requested artifacts (local data and scripts) are proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits runtime actions to searching the included CSV data and generating design systems via the provided scripts (e.g., scripts/search.py). It does not instruct the agent to read unrelated system files, request secrets, or call external endpoints in the visible instructions. The workflow is focused on design-generation and implementation guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only install), so nothing will be downloaded or written to disk by an automated installer. The only runtime behavior is executing local Python scripts that come bundled with the skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That matches the described offline/local nature of the design knowledge base and scripts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and uses normal autonomous invocation defaults. It does not request elevated platform privileges in its manifest. Because it bundles executable scripts, you should consider whether to allow autonomous execution, but the manifest does not grant unusual persistence or cross-skill modification.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and appropriate for generating design systems and mapping them into UI code: it bundles a local knowledge base and Python scripts that implement search and design-system generation. Before installing or enabling autonomous execution, do these quick checks: 1) open scripts/core.py, scripts/search.py, and scripts/design_system.py and search for network-related calls (requests, urllib, socket, httpx, ftplib, subprocess that invokes curl/wget, or hard-coded URLs) and any code that reads files outside the skill folder; 2) confirm the SKILL.md contains no hidden directives that would try to override agent prompts (the pre-scan flag flagged this); 3) if you plan to let the agent run code autonomously, restrict or audit that capability until you’re comfortable—bundled scripts will run with whatever file access the agent has. If you find network calls or attempts to read system config/credentials, treat that as a red flag and do not enable autonomous execution.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: A pre-scan flagged 'system-prompt-override' in SKILL.md. The visible SKILL.md content here contains standard workflow/instructions and no obvious system-prompt override directives; this may be a false positive from pattern matching. Still, treat it as a prompt-injection warning and manually inspect SKILL.md and the script files for hidden or embedded control tokens before granting autonomous execution.
